question: Which type of semiconductor has an excess of holes?
solution:
The correct answer is 1

__Explanation:__

The extrinsic semiconductor can be classified into P-type and N-type based on the majority charge carrier 

__
 
• P-type semiconductor: A semiconductor having holes as majority charge carriers and electrons as minority charge carriers is called a P-type semiconductor.
 
• N-type semiconductor: A semiconductor having electrons as majority charge carriers and holes as minority charge carriers is called an N-type semiconductor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Extrinsic P-type Semiconductor is formed when a trivalent impurity is added to a pure semiconductor
 
• Example of trivalent impurity are Boron, Gallium, and Indium
 
• Trivalent impurity like boron, have 3 valence electrons.
 
• Each atom of the impurity fits in the silicon crystal by forming covalent bonds with the surrounding silicon atoms
 
• The dopant boron atom has one less electron than surrounding silicon and thus vacancy is generated that acts as a hole
